issues.description: The grammar note says adverbs and time phrases like 'every morning' usually go before the main verb, but in the dialogue 'every morning' comes at the end. This could confuse an A2 learner about word order.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the note to: Adverbs of frequency like 'usually' usually go before the main verb. Time phrases like 'every morning' usually go at the end or beginning of the sentence.

issues.description: The English line begins by addressing Ben, but the Vietnamese translation leaves out the name.
issues.suggested_fix: Ben ơi, bạn có thường đi làm bằng xe máy không?

issues.description: The Vietnamese line is understandable, but 'mình đi xe máy mỗi sáng' sounds a little literal. A more natural spoken pattern is 'sáng nào ... cũng'.
issues.suggested_fix: Ừ, sáng nào mình cũng đi xe máy.

issues.description: The English gloss for 'motorbike' is strange and may be unclear for A2 learners. A bike with an engine is clearer.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the English gloss to: a bike with an engine; keep the Vietnamese gloss: xe máy.

qa_report.summary: The micro-dialogue is short, clear, and suitable for A2 learners. The Vietnamese is mostly understandable and natural, but I would make small edits before recording. The most important fix is the grammar note, because it could teach the wrong position for 'every morning'. Also, add the missing name in s1l1, make s1l2 sound more natural, and simplify the English gloss for 'motorbike'.
